title: Destroyers Announce 2025–26 Pre-Season Training Camp at APSU Stadium
summary: Captain Akhil Mishra leads a 43-man expanded training camp ahead of the fifth edition of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament.
body:
Rewa, MP — Destroyers Cricket Club (DES) have formally launched their pre-season preparation for the 2025 and 2026 Atal Bihari Vajpayee Memorial Tournament cycles, assembling a formidable 43-player training contingent at Awadhesh Pratap Singh University (APSU) Stadium.

Skipper Akhil Mishra, who has amassed 905 runs across 19 derby fixtures against arch-rivals Dread Eleven (DE), underscored the franchise’s commitment to reclaiming the tournament crown they previously secured in August 2022.

"Our rivalry with Dread Eleven has evolved into the definitive trial fixture of Vindhya cricket," Mishra remarked during Monday morning’s net session. "With Kuldeep Sen, Kumar Kartikeya, and Ashwin Das spearheading our pace and spin departments, the standard at training has been exceptional."

The upcoming 2025 series will commence with an initial four-match T20 series in September 2025, followed by the Silver Jubilee Tournament edition scheduled for autumn 2026 under the auspices of the Rewa Division Cricket Association (RDCA).

title: Championship Retrospective: Inside Destroyers’ 2022 Final Triumph Over Dread Eleven
summary: A tactical breakdown of the historic 12 August 2022 final where Destroyers defended 183 to hoist the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Trophy.
body:
On 12 August 2022, over 4,500 supporters packed APSU Stadium for what remains the most consequential clash in Rewa divisional cricket history: the 2022 Atal Bihari Vajpayee Tournament Final between Destroyers Cricket Club and Dread Eleven.

Entering the match under immense scrutiny, Destroyers opted to bat first on a rock-hard surface. Pacer Kuldeep Sen delivered a career-defining cameo, blasting 46 runs off just 30 deliveries (4 fours, 3 towering sixes) from the middle order. Coupled with Saransh Surana’s brisk 38 off 25 balls, Destroyers posted a challenging 183 all out.

In response, Dread Eleven mounted a fierce chase spearheaded by star all-rounder Pranav Dwivedi, whose classy 68 kept Dread Eleven in the contest until the 16th over. However, disciplined death bowling from Ashwin Das and spin strangulation from Kumar Kartikeya stemmed the boundary flow, sealing a 21-run victory for Destroyers.

title: RDCA Unveils Upgraded Turf Pitches at APSU Stadium for 2025–2026 Cycle
summary: The Rewa Division Cricket Association completes major renovations to pitch blocks and pavilion facilities ahead of upcoming fixtures.
body:
Rewa — The Rewa Division Cricket Association (RDCA) has officially concluded extensive rejuvenation work across the five-strip central pitch square at APSU Stadium, ensuring international-standard bounce and seam movement for the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

Chief Curator Rajesh Patel confirmed that local red soil combined with clay blends from the Narmada basin was utilized to reinforce the wickets against weathering while ensuring equitable contest between bat and ball.

"Both Destroyers and Dread Eleven showcase fast-paced, modern cricket. These revamped surfaces will reward authentic strokeplay while granting genuine pace bowlers true carry through to the wicketkeeper," Patel stated.

title: Milestone: Akhil Mishra Becomes First Destroyer to Cross 900 Runs Against Dread Eleven
summary: Across 19 hard-fought battles, the Destroyers skipper has set an unprecedented standard of consistency in Rewa cricket.
body:
With an average of 47.63 and 9 half-centuries across 19 innings, Destroyers skipper Akhil Mishra has etched his name into the annals of Rewa cricket as the franchise’s premier run accumulator.

Mishra reached the 900-run plateau during the 2024 50-Over series, maintaining an exceptional strike rate of 107.6 across both T20 and ODI formats. His calm temperament at the crease has repeatedly steadied Destroyers during high-pressure chases.

"Records are satisfying, but victories for Destroyers are all that matter," said Mishra. "We look forward to raising the bar even higher in the 2025 and 2026 fixtures."
